Circuitborn. Normalized Bad Eden ancestry root.

Select one heritage separately when building the character: Exo-Knight, Parallax, Salvage, Synapse.

This root grants the shared Circuitborn core trait package (Firmware of Identity) and preserves live UUID compatibility for the four Line items.

“You are not a robot. You are a decision the world keeps making about itself. The networks are alive and they recognize you on sight.”

Firmware of Identity. You do not eat, drink, or sleep. You enter maintenance trance when you rest. You reroll the lowest die on checks against poison and disease, and you are immune to magical sleep.

Attention Resonance. 1/Soma Break, when a creature you can see is intensely focused on you, you may regain either one spent Bad Eden OP (a category you used this scene) or Integrity equal to your tier.

Informational Matrix Sense. You can feel active networks: radio, signal, ritual, rumor.

Line Memory. Choose one Circuitborn line (Exo-Knight, Parallax, Salvage, Synapse). Your line grants Tier powers as you level.

“You don’t use the network. The network uses you, and that’s the only relationship that doesn’t collapse.”

Synapse. You are a sentient chassis built around the principle of inference. Information is your home. Other people travel through it. You live there.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Construct-Living).
  • Chassis Lean. Your chassis is built around MND (Mind)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.
  • Predictive Cache. 1/Soma Break, when an enemy you can see takes an action, you may have anticipated it: reroll the lowest die on the next reaction or attack you make against that enemy this round.

“Reality is a database. You brought admin tools.”

Yesod-Diver. You reroll the lowest die on checks to interpret metaphysical constructs (Sparks, slippage, noospheric entities). 1/Soma Break, you can ask the GM one direct question about a nearby “system,” and receive a truthful but incomplete answer.

"Strike the clause. Insert your own. Reality reads from the top."

The Cosmic Linguist edits reality like text — meaning first, matter second. One currency now: Surge. The editor always has the next word, so you bank +1 Surge at the start of your turn (the old Resonance, Strain, and Editorial Authority pools are folded into this single pool).

The Edit (spent via Surge)

  • Emphasis (1) — your next Strike or manifestation hits for +Tier d6 (the word, underlined).
  • Stabilize (2) — you gain DR equal to Tier; your next cast resists counter / dispel (the sentence holds).
  • Impose a Reading (3) — a foe's next attack and its saves are at disadvantage (only one correct interpretation: yours).
  • Rewrite the Sentence (5) — a foe loses its reactions and rolls saves at disadvantage; allies near you bank a reroll.

The Sentence endures as your signature stance — while held, the manifestation's primary target is bound by name and rolls its checks against you at disadvantage.

description.value:
“Magic is grammar. Reality is a draft.”

You are a prepared, academic manifestant who edits meaning directly. You do not delegate power; you channel it raw.

Esoteric OS Integration: Your manifesting interacts with correspondences (school ↔ sephirah, day/slot timing). Alignment yields Resonance; misalignment accumulates Strain.

Curated List (doc-only): Cosmic Linguists favor semantic leverage, control, ritual work, and correspondence-aligned craft.

⚙ ENGINE NOTE — the Resonance Pool is now Resonance Channel dice, spent INSIDE the Cast dialog (the ✦ Resonance Channels row: +save DC / +damage die / +duration / defense impose / stabilize). Editorial Authority's Edits live in the ◆ Surge menu.

Resonance Dice (shared pool): You gain Resonance when you cast in correspondence-aligned timing or complete proper ritual work. You may spend Resonance to increase potency (see Resonance Channel).

Strain (shared meter): You gain Strain when you cast misaligned, overcharge effects, or force semantic contradictions. At thresholds, the GM triggers Backlash: reality glitches, psychic recoil, or narrative consequences.

Wizards get to be powerful. Wizards also pay the bill.

🔮 CLASS RESOURCE: Resonance

Type: Dice-based resource pool
Purpose: Measures alignment with reality’s underlying structure

Resonance Dice

  • Start as d6

  • Increase at:

    • Level 5 → d8

    • Level 11 → d10

    • Level 17 → d12

  • Maximum stored dice:
    = your Mind modifier (minimum 1)

Gaining Resonance

You gain 1 Resonance Die when:

  • You cast a manifestation in correct esoteric alignment

  • You complete a properly prepared ritual

  • You exploit an established semantic pattern

  • Your subclass leverages symbolism, structure, or constraint

Limit:
You may gain only 1 Resonance Die per round.

Resonance decays quickly — it is momentum, not savings.

Spending Resonance

When you spend a Resonance Die, roll it and apply one effect:

  • Add the result to a Resolve DC

  • Add an extra damage or effect die

  • Extend duration or scope

  • Impose roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on a defense checks

  • Stabilize a manifestation against countering

Each die spent may generate Strain.

⚠ PUSHBACK SYSTEM: Strain

Type: Escalating consequence meter
Purpose: Measures damage to reality from forced edits

Gaining Strain

You gain +1 Strain when:

  • Casting while misaligned

  • Spending Resonance aggressively

  • Forcing contradictory meanings

  • Using certain subclass features

Some abilities add Strain automatically.

Strain Thresholds (Recommended)

  • 1–2: Cosmetic anomalies, sensory bleed

  • 3–4: Psychic damage, manifestation distortion

  • 5–6: Reality glitches, hostile manifestations

  • 7+: GM-controlled backlash

Clearing Strain

  • Rest

  • Downtime

  • Careful ritual casting

  • Annotator features

  • Pactkeeper intervention

Strain is dangerous but manageable.

🧠 SUMMARY FOR PLAYERS

  • Pactkeepers manage authority

  • Cosmic Linguists manage momentum

  • Jurisdiction = what you are allowed to touch

  • Civic Charge = permission you spend

  • Precedent = what now matters

  • Resonance = how hard you push

  • Strain = what it costs

Nothing here is vague.
Nothing here is hand-wavy.
Everything can be adjudicated at the table consistently.

description.value:
"It is not there anymore. It was never there."

Doctrine: Power lies in omission, silence, and removal — a good redaction is terrifying because it leaves clean edges. Ask what word, path, memory, or option disappears.

The Redactor wins by deletion. Your Surge spends remove things from the sentence: an affliction off an ally, a foe's options, or the foe's entire standing as a threat.

Doctrine (spent via Surge)

  • Redact (1) — strike one condition off an ally (clean edges where it used to be).
  • Silence (2) — a foe cannot take reactions until your next turn (its options, omitted).
  • Erasure (5) — a foe is Staggered, cannot take reactions, and rolls its saves at disadvantage (struck from the sentence).

“You already know. You just refuse to say it too early.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The High Priestess (Seer). You read the invisible pressure in a room before anyone else admits it exists. You are intuition weaponized, omen-bearing, and very difficult to surprise in ways that matter.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your archetype sharpens the faction’s hidden-state awareness and information leverage. This Archetype is associated with +1 Intrigue in faction calculus in Bad Eden’s faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for your full tactical and strategic toolkit; those are granted automatically by the Tier Engine at the appropriate character levels.

attributes (Archetype ASI)

When you choose this Archetype, you gain 3 attribute points to distribute using the 2024 rules (no more than +2 to any one score). Common patterns include:

  • Watcher of Omens: +2 Soul, +1 Mind
  • Reader of Motives: +2 Soul, +1 Presence
  • Silent Oracle: +1 Soul, +1 Mind, +1 Presence

These are suggestions, not restraints. Any valid 3-point distribution is allowed.

description.value:
Crew Type (Bad Eden): Abyssal Cartographers.

“There are maps beneath the map.”

Abyssal Cartographers chart what most people refuse to admit exists: drowned tunnels, pressure-cut caverns, forgotten ferry lines, and the strange geometry of places where water remembers older routes than roads do. They do not merely travel hidden ways. They prove those ways were always there.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Investigation.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Intrigue OPs.

Soul - Creative energy. +1 Violence, +1 Soft Power OPs

Creation arrives all at once. Chokmah rewards decisive action, inspired leadership, and bold openers that turn possibility into momentum before anyone else is ready.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Alchemist.

“Reality is a solvent. I’m the one shaking the bottle.”

Alchemists do not seek purity. They seek conversion.

Where others pursue the Great Work through revelation, alignment, or doctrine, the Alchemist treats it as a throughput problem. Matter, belief, institutions, and people are all half-finished reactions waiting for the right catalyst.

An Alchemist does not ask what should this be? They ask what can I turn this into before it detonates?

They stabilize supply chains with miracles, turn contamination into leverage, and force abundance out of systems that should already have collapsed. Nothing they do is free. Every refinement leaves residue.

How Alchemists pursue the Great Work:

  • By converting one form of value into another
  • By stabilizing volatile systems just long enough to matter
  • By treating Sparks, OPs, and infrastructure as reactive states
  • By accepting that every solution leaves chemical, moral, or metaphysical residue

Resonance: Yesod — foundation, transfer, containment, and the unstable bridge between idea and matter.

Tell-tales: antiseptic, ozone, burnt sugar, stained gloves, reinforced glass where glass should not survive.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 to Economy OP rolls (especially production, infrastructure, and supply stabilization)

Cost Principle: Alchemical victories leave residue. Expect shortages, contamination, attention, moral debt, or unstable downstream consequences when you push too hard.

description.value:
Tier 1 — Abyssal Cartographers

“There are maps beneath the map.”

Abyssal Cartographers chart what most people refuse to admit exists: drowned tunnels, pressure-cut caverns, forgotten ferry lines, and the strange geometry of places where water remembers older routes than roads do. They do not merely travel hidden ways. They prove those ways were always there.

You’ve learned the first law of deep travel: the visible route is usually the stupid one.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Investigation.
  • Strategic: In River, Lake, Sea, Ocean, or Cavern-adjacent routes, discovery and route-finding are more reliable.

Tier 1 — Alchemist

“You’re not powerful yet. You’re noticeable.”

At Tier 1, you learn the first dangerous lesson: matter listens.

You are not generating value yet. You are accelerating reactions, shortening timelines, and making crude but effective substitutions when a system would otherwise stall out.

People start bringing you problems that smell like “this should not work.”

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank with the Occult aptitude
  • When crafting basic alchemical items, the time required is halved
  • You can identify substances, compounds, and chemical hazards in minutes instead of hours

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • Production Reliability: once per Strategic Turn, when your faction spends Economy OP on production, infrastructure, or supply stabilization, reduce that spend by 1 (minimum 1)

Cost: every use leaves evidence — fumes, scarcity elsewhere, suspicious efficiency, or a process that now depends on you.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Production Reliability
Recovery: 1/Strategic Turn  ·  Action: Strategic  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
When faction spends Economy OP on production / infrastructure / supply, reduce spend by 1 (min 1).

Once per Soma Break, when you remove or negate something, you may declare:

Total Redaction.

Within scope:

  • Summons cannot be re-summoned by that source for a time.

  • Curses cannot reattach.

  • Teleport anchors fail.

  • Reanimation attempts collapse.

This does not:

  • Erase canon.

  • Kill immortals.

  • Undo narrative Lore.

It enforces finality within your jurisdiction.

Major Strain.
Backlash guaranteed.

Redactors don’t erase existence.

They erase permissions.

3rd Level)

Names matter. You remove them.

Once per Soma Break:

Choose a creature or effect and strip one semantic label:

  • Undead

  • Summoned

  • Magical

  • Hostile

  • Protected

  • Etc.

For a short duration, abilities that rely on that label:

  • Fail

  • Treat the target as invalid

  • Lose their trigger condition

This is loud magic.

Gain Strain immediately.

You did not change the thing.

You changed what it counts as.

Undyed sept-cloth cut to a long working robe with a corded belt. Issued to first-circle initiates of any chapterhouse or tutor-cell — the kind of garment that gets traded between students faster than any of them keep notebooks. Comfortable to channel in. Forgettable to anyone watching for trouble.

Standard Issue. Light enough to manifest in. Dignified enough to walk past a sept-warden.

system.flavor: She murmured one sentence. The story acquired a margin.

manifestation.concept: You append a small reading to a recent event — a footnote — that the room must now consider true alongside the original.
manifestation.durationText: The footnote stays attached for the rest of the scene.
manifestation.riskText: If your footnote contradicts a witnessed truth too brazenly, the footnote tears and you take 1 Noise.
manifestation.pathResonance: Cosmic Linguist (Annotator) — small surgical edit, large consequence.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You don't change what happened. You change how the room is allowed to read what happened.
manifestation.gmCalibration: T1 Working. One sentence. GM and player negotiate exact wording.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Add one fact, motive, or implication to a recent event. Anyone present must reroll their lowest die on the next check that depends on understanding the event.
manifestation.signature: A faint asterisk hovers over the event you have annotated. Not everyone sees it; everyone who reads sees it.
manifestation.thirdThing: Other Linguists can read your footnotes. They will know who wrote it.

system.flavor: He italicized a single word. The argument bent around it.

manifestation.concept: Your next utterance lands as inarguable. Not a compulsion — a perfect formatting of meaning. The thing you said is now what was said.
manifestation.riskText: You cannot use this to force compliance. If you try, the emphasis fails and you take 1 Stress.
manifestation.pathResonance: Cosmic Linguist (Metaphor Apostle) — the said becomes the case.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You speak in italics. The room copies it down.
manifestation.gmCalibration: T1 Working. One sentence. NPCs may still disagree — they cannot pretend they didn't hear it.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Your next single statement (one sentence) is treated by the scene as common knowledge. Allies reroll lowest die on the next roll predicated on agreeing with you.
manifestation.signature: Your voice momentarily acquires an italic quality — slightly slanted, slightly warmer.
manifestation.thirdThing: The emphasized statement is remembered with perfect verbatim accuracy by everyone in the scene, even if they would prefer not to.

system.flavor: She licked her thumb. She turned a page. The word became something else.

manifestation.concept: A small book or sheaf of pages bound to your hand. It updates itself as you read. Definitions are slightly malleable in your favor.
manifestation.riskText: If destroyed, you lose access to your last 1d4 Workings until a new glossary is begun. Reading rival glossaries can corrupt yours.
manifestation.pathResonance: Cosmic Linguist (Annotator) — meaning under your continuous editing.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can change what a word means. Quietly. The room follows.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier-1 Form. Visible to other Linguists. Useless if you cannot read the language being spoken.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Once per scene, redefine a single word in the conversation. The redefinition holds for the scene. +2 to Insight rolls while open.
manifestation.signature: Pages turn when you turn your attention. The handwriting is yours and not yours.
manifestation.thirdThing: The glossary records your every working, even those you have not yet performed.

system.effect: Write a tiny correction in the margin of an event that is happening too soon. The thing still happens, but it loses certainty, timing, or emphasis.
system.flavor: Invisible punctuation flares around the edited event.

manifestation.concept: A surgical editorial delay imposed on one unfolding action, claim, or consequence.
manifestation.costText: 1 Clarity. You must actually understand what sentence of reality you're editing.
manifestation.durationText: Until the end of the current exchange or the next clean beat.
manifestation.triggerText: Best used in response to an attack, declaration, alarm, or sudden movement.
manifestation.targetText: One action, one attack, one spoken declaration, or one consequence about to land.
manifestation.rangeAreaText: Sight, hearing, or a text-like symbolic connection.
manifestation.riskText: Reality resents public copy-editing; deleted momentum may come back cranky.
manifestation.pathResonance: Cosmic Linguist / Annotator doctrine / modest edit, large consequence.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can delay, soften, footnote, or partially reframe something that is already trying to happen.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Let it buy timing, ambiguity, or reduction—not total negation unless the setup was exquisite.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Reaction-speed delay or deflection effect for one event.
manifestation.signature: A tiny glowing caret appears over the thing being corrected.
manifestation.thirdThing: Every use leaves one innocent word in the scene slightly out of place.

system.flavor: He looked at the door. The margins of the door began to fill in.

manifestation.concept: A field of slow, drifting margins around a person, place, or object. Annotations accumulate around it whether or not anyone is writing.
manifestation.riskText: Other Linguists can read your marginalia. Annotation reveals the annotator.
manifestation.pathResonance: Cosmic Linguist (Archivist) — past and future as marginalia of the present.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can study a thing the way a scholar studies a manuscript. The thing knows.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier-2 Form. Visible to anyone with second sight. Excellent for investigation; expensive for action.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: While active on a target, every Insight, Investigate, or Recall roll about the target rerolls the lowest die. Once per scene, ask the GM one question about the target — they answer truthfully but minimally.
manifestation.signature: Light, almost-readable script drifts in the air at the edge of vision around the marked subject.
manifestation.thirdThing: The accumulated annotations include things no one has yet observed. The future leaks through.

system.flavor: It scuttled under the door. It came back with the answer.

manifestation.concept: A small inkling — half ink-blot, half insect — that copies what you observe. It can be sent ahead to read for you.
manifestation.riskText: If captured by another Linguist, they can read your recent Workings.
manifestation.pathResonance: Cosmic Linguist (Archivist) — observation as ongoing record.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You have a small, smart, mostly-silent helper that reads on your behalf.
manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier-1 Form. Easily missed; easily destroyed by anyone paying attention. GM may grant it a small personality.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Send the familiar Far range to scout. It returns with a single accurate sentence about what it saw. Once per scene, it may copy a written page verbatim.
manifestation.signature: It moves silently. It leaves a faint trail of ink that evaporates.
manifestation.thirdThing: It cannot lie to you, but it can choose what to mention first. It has preferences.

system.flavor: He drew a line through what he had just said. They forgot. He did not.

manifestation.concept: You delete a recent sentence — a thing said, a thing acted, a thing recorded — from the canon of the scene. It happened. It is no longer the case that it happened.
manifestation.durationText: Permanent — until someone else writes the moment back in.
manifestation.riskText: Major edits draw attention from other Linguists, archivists, and any reality-stable witness (some saints, some children, some Pactkeepers).
manifestation.pathResonance: Cosmic Linguist (Redactor) — power lies in clean omission.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can take back a word that has already been said. Reality cooperates. Mostly.
manifestation.gmCalibration: T2 Working. Cannot delete events that constitute the spine of the scene. GM may require a higher tier for that.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Erase one specific action, statement, or observation from the last 60 seconds. People in the scene revise their memory. Hard evidence (writing, recording) develops a flaw or smudge.
manifestation.signature: The deleted moment leaves a thin line through the air, a visible strikethrough that fades over the next minute.
manifestation.thirdThing: The deleted moment still happened in the deleter's memory. You will remember it forever, even if no one else does.

manifestation.concept: Edit the target's most recent memories to something distracting, causing them to lose focus on their current activity.
